summary: Iteration 1: End-to-end backend + frontend smoke test of RustAdmin remote-access management panel. Discovered and fixed two MongoDB ObjectId leakage bugs (POST /api/address-book and GET /api/server-config returning 500). After fixes, ALL 15 backend pytest cases pass (auth, dashboard, devices CRUD/heartbeat/search/filter, sessions lifecycle + offline guard, users CRUD with admin-only RBAC verified via real operator login, audit log prefix filter, access tokens, address book, server config). Frontend login + navigation across all 8 sidebar pages (Dashboard, Devices, Sessions, Address Book, Audit Logs, Users, Access Tokens, Settings) works without errors; Devices Connect modal opens with the mocked live-preview image and 'Encerrar sessão' button.

minor.issue: Was returning 500 due to ObjectId leak (`return {**doc}` after motor insert_one mutated doc). FIXED by popping `_id` before return.
Was returning 500 on first-ever call (no row yet) because default cfg inserted then returned still had injected `_id`. FIXED by popping `_id` after insert.

issues: Recharts console warning: ResponsiveContainer reports width(-1)/height(-1). Likely parent has no explicit min-height on initial render before metrics load. Charts do eventually render once data arrives; consider adding minHeight on the chart wrapper to silence the warning and avoid layout flash.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Add minHeight to dashboard ResponsiveContainer wrappers to remove recharts width/height(-1) console warnings.

OPTIONAL: backend/.env has CORS_ORIGINS="*" but server.py ignores it and hard-codes [FRONTEND_URL, http://localhost:3000]. Production FRONTEND_URL in backend/.env (aeecbd55-...) differs from the active REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL host (remote-access-hub-18...). Browser flows still work because the same Kubernetes ingress is used and credentialed requests came through OK, but consider syncing FRONTEND_URL with the current preview host to avoid future CORS surprises.
critical_code_review_comments: MongoDB ObjectId leak pattern: Anywhere code returns a doc immediately after motor `insert_one`, the dict gets a non-serializable `_id` field. Found 2 occurrences (now fixed). Recommend wrapping inserts in a small helper that strips `_id` post-insert, or always re-fetching with `{_id: 0}` projection.

Lockout fixture: `login_attempts` uses `ip:email` identifier and 15-min lockout. Tests for invalid login use unique emails to avoid blocking admin. Verify production rate-limiter doesn't lock real users out unexpectedly during legitimate retries.
server.py is ~720 lines; per code-review guideline (>700 lines) splitting into modules (auth.py, devices.py, sessions.py, etc.) would improve maintainability.

success_rate.frontend: 100% smoke (login + all 8 nav pages + connect modal)

seed_data_creation: Seed data verified: 10 devices, multiple sessions (1 active + 6 ended), 10+ audit logs auto-created on startup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend stable at 15/15. Mocked items (per request): bandwidth_series random data, Connect modal shows static image. No real WebRTC. Auth uses httpOnly cookies + Authorization Bearer fallback (tests use Bearer to bypass cookie-domain quirks). FRONTEND_URL in backend/.env != REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL but CORS still permissive enough for current preview.
rca of the issue: Both 500 errors had identical RCA — motor's `insert_one(doc)` mutates the passed dict in-place by adding an `ObjectId _id`. The two endpoints then returned that mutated dict directly (`return {**doc}` / `return cfg`), bypassing the usual `find_one(..., {'_id': 0})` projection guard. FastAPI's jsonable_encoder failed with `TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable`. Fix: pop `_id` from the dict after insert before returning. Reproduction: hit POST /api/address-book or GET /api/server-config on a fresh DB. Mitigation applied + verified via pytest re-run.
